Implement the following plan:

# Spotify API Compatibility Update

## Context

SmarterPlaylists was originally built against the Spotify + Echo Nest APIs circa 2016. Several Spotify API endpoints and spotipy library methods have been deprecated since then. The Echo Nest API was shut down entirely in 2016. This plan updates all API integration to current Spotify Web API standards (2026) to prevent future breakage.

---

## Phase 1: Backend — `pbl/pbl/spotify_plugs.py`

### 1a. Update deprecated spotipy method calls

| Line | Old | New |
|------|-----|-----|
| 145 | `_get_spotify().user_playlists(user)` | `_get_spotify().user_playlists(user)` — keep as-is, used for arbitrary users |
| 374 | `_, _, user, _, pid = self.uri.split(':')` | Handle both 3-part and 5-part URI formats |
| 391 | `sp.user_playlist_create(self.user, ...)` | `sp.user_playlist_create(self.user, ...)` — still works in spotipy 2.23+ |
| 401 | `sp.user_playlist_replace_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_replace_items(pid, turis)` |
| 404 | `sp.user_playlist_add_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_add_items(pid, turis)` |
| 435 | `sp.user_playlists(user, ...)` | `sp.current_user_playlists(...)` |

### 1b. Fix `_save_playlist` URI parsing (line 374)

Currently assumes old 5-part format `spotify:user:X:playlist:Y`. Update to handle both:
```python
parts = self.uri.split(':')
if len(parts) == 5:
    _, _, user, _, pid = parts
elif len(parts) == 3:
    _, _, pid = parts
    user = self.user
```

Also fix line 393 which does `uri.split(':')[4]` — same issue.

### 1c. Update `normalize_uri()` (line 616)

Modern Spotify URLs are `https://open.spotify.com/playlist/Y` (no user segment). After URL→URI conversion, normalize old 5-part playlist URIs to 3-part:
```python
# After URL conversion, normalize old playlist URIs
parts = uri.split(':')
if len(parts) == 5 and parts[0] == 'spotify' and parts[1] == 'user' and parts[3] == 'playlist':
    uri = 'spotify:playlist:' + parts[4]
```

### 1d. Safe access for deprecated response fields (lines 490, 565, 573)

Use `.get()` with defaults for `popularity` (deprecated by Spotify):
- `track.get('popularity', 0)`
- `album.get('popularity', 0)`
- `artist.get('popularity', 0)`

---

## Phase 2: Backend — `app/server/plugs.py`

### 2a. Replace deprecated spotipy calls

| Line | Old | New |
|------|-----|-----|
| 445 | `sp.user_playlist_replace_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_replace_items(pid, turis)` |
| 447 | `sp.user_playlist_add_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_add_items(pid, turis)` |
| 519 | `sp.user_playlist_add_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_add_items(pid, turis)` |
| 573 | `sp.user_playlist_replace_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_replace_items(pid, turis)` |
| 575 | `sp.user_playlist_add_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_add_items(pid, turis)` |
| 767 | `get_spotify().user_playlists(user)` | `get_spotify().current_user_playlists()` |
| 782 | `get_spotify().user_playlist_tracks(user, playlist_id, ...)` | `get_spotify().playlist_items(playlist_id, ...)` |
| 899 | `get_spotify().user_playlists(user)` | `get_spotify().current_user_playlists()` |
| 915 | `get_spotify().user_playlist_tracks(user, playlist_id, ...)` | `get_spotify().playlist_items(playlist_id, ...)` |

Note: `user_playlist_create` (lines 435, 510, 559) still works in spotipy 2.23+ — keep as-is.

---

## Phase 3: Frontend — `app/web/callback.html`

### 3a. Update API endpoint URLs

| Line | Old | New |
|------|-----|-----|
| 30 | `/v1/users/{username}/playlists` | `/v1/me/playlists` |
| 53-55 | `/v1/users/{username}/playlists/{pid}/tracks` | `/v1/playlists/{pid}/tracks` |
| 87-88 | `/v1/users/{username}/playlists/{pid}/tracks` | `/v1/playlists/{pid}/tracks` |

### 3b. Fix URI construction (line 138)

Old: `'spotify:user:' + username + ':playlist:' + pid`
New: `'spotify:playlist:' + pid`

Also update the link to use web URL: `'https://open.spotify.com/playlist/' + pid`

### 3c. Fix `doit()` URI parsing (lines 188-190)

Handle both old 5-part and new 3-part URI formats when extracting pid from `g_uri`.

---

## Phase 4: Frontend — `app/web/playlist.js`

### 4a. Handle deprecated `preview_url` gracefully (lines 53-63)

`preview_url` is deprecated and may be `null`. Add null check before calling `play()`:
```javascript
if (track.spotify && track.spotify.preview_url) {
    play(track.spotify.preview_url);
} else {
    fetchSpotifyTrackInfo(track.id, function(info) {
        if (info && info.preview_url) {
            track.spotify = info;
            play(info.preview_url);
        }
        // silently fail if no preview available
    });
}
```

### 4b. Fix `fetchSpotifyTrackInfo` (line 70-78)

This calls `GET /v1/tracks/{tid}` without auth — will fail. Add auth header using stored token, or remove this function since previews are unreliable now anyway.

### 4c. Remove deprecated implicit grant `loginWithSpotify` (lines 86-92)

Uses `response_type=token` (Implicit Grant, deprecated by Spotify). This function is unused by the main app — the auth flow uses `main.js`'s `loginWithSpotifyForAuth()` instead. Remove or mark as deprecated.

---

## Phase 5: Echo Nest Cleanup

### 5a. `pbl/pbl/echonest_plugs.py`

- **Comment out** the annotator registration at line 225: `tlib.add_annotator(_echonest_annotator)` — this registers a non-functional annotator that will fail when called
- Guard the `import pyen` with try/except so removal of pyen from requirements doesn't break imports
- Keep class definitions so existing saved programs get clear errors instead of import failures

### 5b. `app/server/components.py`

- Echo Nest components (EchoNestGenreRadio, EchoNestArtistRadio, EchoNestArtist) already have `'disabled': True` — no change needed
- Remove `"echonest"` from the annotations type list (around line 36) since it's non-functional

---

## Phase 6: Frontend Scopes — `app/web/main.js` + `main2.js`

- Fix duplicate `user-follow-read` scope (appears twice, lines 439-440)
- Optionally add `user-read-recently-played` scope

---

## Phase 7: `requirements.txt`

- Keep `spotipy>=2.23,<3.0` (already correct)
- Keep `pyen>=0.3` for now (echonest_plugs.py still imports it at module level; guarded with try/except in Phase 5)

---

## Files to Modify

1. `pbl/pbl/spotify_plugs.py` — deprecated spotipy methods, URI handling, deprecated fields
2. `app/server/plugs.py` — deprecated spotipy methods (12 call sites)
3. `app/web/callback.html` — old Spotify API endpoints, old URI format
4. `app/web/playlist.js` — deprecated preview_url, deprecated implicit grant
5. `pbl/pbl/echonest_plugs.py` — disable annotator registration
6. `app/server/components.py` — remove echonest from annotations list
7. `app/web/main.js` — fix duplicate scope
8. `app/web/main2.js` — fix duplicate scope

## Verification

1. Run local import test: `.venv/bin/python -c "import pbl; import components; import compiler; import plugs"` to verify no import errors
2. Rebuild Docker image and deploy to Synology
3. Test: login → create a simple playlist program → save → run → verify playlist appears in Spotify
4. Test: load existing program from directory → run
5. Check Docker logs for any Python errors after each operation


If you need specific details from before exiting plan mode (like exact code snippets, error messages, or content you generated), read the full transcript at: /Users/brunobrunkow/.claude/projects/-Users-brunobrunkow-Downloads-SmarterPlaylists-master/874374ff-713d-4b6f-a973-b0f127abc4ea.jsonl

        params = { 'type': 'artist', 'artist': artist, 'results': int(count) }
        super(EchoNestArtistPlaylist, self).__init__('Artist playlist for ' + artist, params)


def _annotate_tracks_with_echonest_data(tids):
    otids = tlib.annotate_tracks_from_cache('echonest', tids)
    if len(otids) > 0:
        stids = set(otids)
        uris = [ 'spotify:track:' + tid for tid in otids]
        try:
            if debug:
                print('getting echonest info for', otids)
            response = _get_en().get('song/profile', track_id=uris, bucket=_en_song_buckets)
            res = set()
            for song in response['songs']:
                for track in song['tracks']:
                    tid = utils.uri_to_id(track['foreign_id'])
                    if tid in stids:
                        res.add(tid)
                        tlib.annotate_track(tid, 'echonest', _flatten_en_song(song, tid))
            diff = stids - res
            if len(diff) > 0:
                pass
                #print 'requested', len(stids), 'collected', len(res)
        except pyen.PyenException as e:
            print('annotate_tracks_with_echonest_data:no info for', otids)
            print('echonest error', e.http_status, e.code, e.msg)
            for tid in otids:
                tlib.annotate_track(tid, 'echonest', {'empty': 'empty'})
    

def _flatten_en_song(song, id):
    for k,v in song['audio_summary'].items():
        song[k] = v

    if 'artist_foreign_ids' in song:
        del song['artist_foreign_ids']

    if 'audio_summary' in song:
        del song['audio_summary']

    if 'analysis_url' in song:
        del song['analysis_url']

    for track in song['tracks']:
        tid = utils.uri_to_id(track['foreign_id'])
        if id == tid:
            if 'album_name' in track:
                song['album_name'] = track['album_name']
            if 'album_date' in track:
                song['album_date'] = track['album_date']
            if 'album_type' in track:
                song['album_type'] = track['album_type']

    del song['tracks']
    return song

def _add_song(source, song):
    id = utils.uri_to_id(song['tracks'][0]['foreign_id'])
    dur = int(song['audio_summary']['duration'] )
    tlib.make_track(id, song['title'], song['artist_name'], dur, source)
    tlib.annotate_track(id, 'echonest', _flatten_en_song(song, id))
    return id

_echonest_annotator = {
    'name': 'echonest',
    'annotator': _annotate_tracks_with_echonest_data,
    'batch_size': 50
}

def _get_en():
    global en
    if en == None:
        en = pyen.Pyen()
        en.trace = False
    return en

tlib.add_annotator(_echonest_annotator)

Pushed (`d409c6f`). After rebuilding the Docker image, the logs will show lines like:

```
[plugs] playlist_tracks class=DatedPlaylistSource uri=spotify:playlist:37i9dQZEVXbgW2o23eKnnt id=37i9dQZEVXbgW2o23eKnnt offset=0
[plugs] SpotifyException http_status=404 reason=Not Found msg=...
[plugs] spotipy version=2.23.0
```

Key things to check in the output:
1. **spotipy version** — if it's 2.22+, `playlist_tracks()` internally calls `/items`, explaining the URL
2. **http_status** — confirms it's a real 404, not a 401/403 auth issue
3. **msg** — Spotify sometimes returns a more specific reason (e.g. "Non existing id" vs "Resource not found")

If spotipy 2.22+ is confirmed, the likely fix is passing `market='from_token'` — which tells Spotify to use the authenticated user's market, required for editorial/regional playlists.

The Docker container is running on your Synology. SSH in and run:

```bash
# List running containers to find the name
docker ps
```

import sys
import os

_root = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(_root, 'pbl'))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(_root, 'pyen'))

import redis
import program_manager
import time
import simplejson as json
import threading
from datetime import datetime,date

class Scheduler(object):
    '''
        constraints - only one scheduled task per item
        squeue - a zset with proc IDs ('process:pid') sorted by excution times
        proces info a hash with
           pid, next exec time, 
            delta, count, error count, consecutive errors count

        process-stats: a list of json results, trimmed to size 10
        sleeper queue
    '''
    def __init__(self, redis, pm):
        self.r = redis
        self.pm = pm
        self.job_queue = 'sched-job-queue'
        self.proc_queue = 'sched-proc-queue'
        self.wait_queue = 'sched-wait-queue'
        self.max_time = 1000000
        self.max_cerrors = 3
        self.max_retained_results = 5
        self.max_age_results = 40 * 24 * 60 * 60

    def schedule(self, auth_code, user, pid, when, delta, total):
        # as a pipleline
        # add schedule to process info hash
        # if count > 0
        #    add proc-id when to squeue
        #    hash proc info to hash (dec count)
        # post to sleeper queue

        skey = mk_sched_key('job', user, pid)
        pipe = self.r.pipeline()
        pipe.hset(skey, 'auth_code', auth_code)
        pipe.hset(skey, 'user', user)
        pipe.hset(skey, 'pid', pid)
        pipe.hset(skey, 'when', when)
        pipe.hset(skey, 'delta', delta)
        pipe.hset(skey, 'total', total)
        pipe.hset(skey, 'runs', 0)
        pipe.hset(skey, 'errors', 0)
        pipe.hset(skey, 'cerrors', 0)
        pipe.hset(skey, 'status', 'running')
        pipe.execute()
        self.post_job(skey, when)
        return True

    def get_batch_schedule_status(self, user, pids):
        pipe = self.r.pipeline()
        for pid in pids:
            jkey = mk_sched_key('job', user, pid)
            pipe.hgetall(jkey)
        ss = pipe.execute()
        out = {}

        for pid, s in zip(pids,ss):
            if 'pid' in s:
                ps  = self.prep_status(s)
                out[ s['pid' ]] = ps
            else:
                out[pid] = {}
        return out


    def prep_status(self, status):
        skip_fields = set(['auth_code'])
        int_fields = set(['cerrors', 'delta', 'errors', 'next_run',
            'runs', 'total', 'when'])

        out = {}
        for k, v in status.items():
            if k in skip_fields:
                continue
            if k in int_fields:
                v = int(v)
            out[k] = v
        return out
        
    def post_job(self, skey, when):
        print('posting', skey, 'to run in', when - time.time(), 'secs')
        pipe = self.r.pipeline()
        pipe.hset(skey, 'status', 'queued')
        pipe.hset(skey, 'next_run', when)
        pipe.zadd(self.job_queue, when, skey)
        pipe.lpush(self.wait_queue, 1)
        pipe.execute()
        self.pm.inc_global_counter("jobs_posted")

    def cancel(self, user, pid):
        skey = mk_sched_key('job', user, pid)
        self.r.zrem(self.job_queue, skey)
        pipe = self.r.pipeline()
        pipe.hset(skey, 'next_run', 0)
        pipe.hset(skey, 'status', 'stopped')
        pipe.execute()
        self.pm.inc_global_counter("jobs_canceled")
        return True

    def get_run_stats(self, user, pid):
        skey = mk_sched_key('job', user, pid)
        stats = self.r.hgetall(skey)
        return self.prep_status(stats)

    def get_recent_results(self, user, pid):
        rkey = mk_sched_key('results', user, pid)
        results = self.r.lrange(rkey, 0, self.max_retained_results - 1)
        out = []
        for js in results:
            out.append(json.loads(js))
        return out

    def get_next_item(self):
        now = self.now()
        items = self.r.zrange(self.job_queue, 0, 0, withscores=True, score_cast_func=int)
        if len(items) > 0:
            item = items[0]
            skey, next_time = item
            if now >= next_time:
                self.r.zrem(self.job_queue, skey)
                return skey
        else:
            return None

    def get_next_delta(self):
        now = self.now()
        items = self.r.zrange(self.job_queue, 0, 0, withscores=True, score_cast_func=int)
        if len(items) > 0:
            item = items[0]
            skey, next_time = item
            return next_time - now
        else:
            return self.max_time
        
    def wait_for_next(self):
        timeout = self.get_next_delta()
        if timeout > 0:
            print('waiting for', timeout, 'secs')
            self.r.blpop(self.wait_queue, timeout)
        return self.get_next_item()
            
    def execute_job(self, skey):
        results = None
        info = self.r.hgetall(skey)
        print('execute_job', skey, info)
        if info:
            print('execute_job', info)
            auth_code = info['auth_code']
            pid = info['pid']
            results = self.pm.execute_program(auth_code, pid, True)
            self.pm.inc_global_counter("jobs_executed")
        return results

    def run_job(self, skey):
        self.r.hset(skey, 'status', 'running')
        results = self.execute_job(skey)
        if results:
            self.process_job_result(skey, results)

    def process_job_result(self, skey, results):
        p = self.r.pipeline()
        p.hincrby(skey, 'runs', 1)
        if results['status'] == 'ok':
            p.hset(skey, 'cerrors', 0)
        else:
            p.hincrby(skey, 'cerrors', 1)
            p.hincrby(skey, 'errors', 1)
        p.hgetall(skey)
        pres = p.execute()
        info = pres[-1]

        cerrors = int(info['cerrors'])
        runs = int(info['runs'])
        delta = int(info['delta'])

        print()
        print('info', info)
        print()

        user = info['user']
        pid = info['pid']

        results['runtime'] = time.time()
        if cerrors > self.max_cerrors:
            results['info'] = 'max consecutive errors exceeded, job cancelled'
            self.r.hset(skey, 'next_run', 0)
            self.r.hset(skey, 'status', 'cancelled')
            self.pm.inc_global_counter("jobs_max_errors_reached")
        elif runs >= int(info['total']):
            results['info'] = 'total runs reached, job finished'
            self.r.hset(skey, 'status', 'finished')
            self.r.hset(skey, 'next_run', 0)
            self.pm.inc_global_counter("jobs_total_runs_reached")
        elif delta == 0:
            results['info'] = 'run cancelled by user'
            self.r.hset(skey, 'status', 'cancelled')
            self.r.hset(skey, 'next_run', 0)
            self.pm.inc_global_counter("jobs_cancelled_by_user")
        else:
            next_time = self.now() + delta
            next_date = datetime.fromtimestamp(next_time).strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
            results['info'] = 'next run at ' + next_date
            self.post_job(skey, next_time)

        ntracks = len(results['tids']) if 'tids' in results else 0
        results['oinfo'] = 'generated ' + str(ntracks) + ' tracks'
        rkey = mk_sched_key('results', user, pid)
        jresults = json.dumps(results, indent=2)
        # print jresults
        self.r.lpush(rkey, jresults)
        self.r.ltrim(rkey, 0, self.max_retained_results - 1)
        self.r.expire(rkey, self.max_age_results)
        show_results(results)


    def now(self):
        return int(time.time())

    def process_job_queue(self):
        print('starting job pusher')
        while True:
            skey = self.wait_for_next()
            if skey:
                print('    pushing', skey)
                self.r.rpush(self.proc_queue, skey)

    def process_jobs(self):
        print('starting job processor')
        while True:
            _,skey = self.r.blpop(self.proc_queue)
            if skey:
                print('   processing', skey)
                self.run_job(skey)
            else:
                break
        print('shutting down job processor')

    def start_processing_threads(self, threads=5):
        def worker():
            self.process_jobs()

        self.show_info()

        for i in range(threads):
            t = threading.Thread(target=worker)
            t.daemon = True
            t.start()
        sched.process_job_queue()

    def show_info(self):
        count = self.r.zcount(self.job_queue, -sys.maxsize, sys.maxsize)
        print('job queue has', count, 'jobs')

        
def show_results(result):
    try:
        print("%s %s %.2f" % (result['status'], fmt_date(result['runtime']), result['time']))
        print(result['oinfo'])
        print(result['info'])
        if result['status'] == 'ok':
            print(result['name'])
            print(result['uri'])
        else:
            print(result['message'])
        print()
    except:
        raise
        print("trouble showing formatted result")
        print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
        print()

def fmt_date(ts):
    the_date = date.fromtimestamp(ts)
    return the_date.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        
        
def mk_sched_key(op, user, pid):
    return 'sched-' + op + '-' + user + '-' + pid

if __name__ == '__main__':
    import random
    import spotify_auth

    my_redis = redis.StrictRedis(host=os.environ.get('REDIS_HOST', 'localhost'), port=int(os.environ.get('REDIS_PORT', 6379)), db=0, decode_responses=True)
    my_auth = spotify_auth.SpotifyAuth(r=my_redis)
    my_pm = program_manager.ProgramManager(my_auth, r=my_redis)

    sched = Scheduler(my_redis, my_pm)

    threads = 5
    if len(sys.argv) > 1:
        threads = int(sys.argv[1])

    sched.start_processing_threads(threads)

- **`zadd`**: redis-py 4.x requires `{member: score}` dict — the old positional `(score, member)` syntax raises a `TypeError` that would crash the scheduler worker on every job post, causing the restart loop
- **`sched` → `self`**: would have caused a `NameError` at startup when calling `start_processing_threads`

import sys
import os

_root = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(_root, 'pbl'))
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(_root, 'pyen'))

import redis
import program_manager
import time
import simplejson as json
import threading
from datetime import datetime,date

class Scheduler(object):
    '''
        constraints - only one scheduled task per item
        squeue - a zset with proc IDs ('process:pid') sorted by excution times
        proces info a hash with
           pid, next exec time, 
            delta, count, error count, consecutive errors count

        process-stats: a list of json results, trimmed to size 10
        sleeper queue
    '''
    def __init__(self, redis, pm):
        self.r = redis
        self.pm = pm
        self.job_queue = 'sched-job-queue'
        self.proc_queue = 'sched-proc-queue'
        self.wait_queue = 'sched-wait-queue'
        self.max_time = 1000000
        self.max_cerrors = 3
        self.max_retained_results = 5
        self.max_age_results = 40 * 24 * 60 * 60

    def schedule(self, auth_code, user, pid, when, delta, total):
        # as a pipleline
        # add schedule to process info hash
        # if count > 0
        #    add proc-id when to squeue
        #    hash proc info to hash (dec count)
        # post to sleeper queue

        skey = mk_sched_key('job', user, pid)
        pipe = self.r.pipeline()
        pipe.hset(skey, 'auth_code', auth_code)
        pipe.hset(skey, 'user', user)
        pipe.hset(skey, 'pid', pid)
        pipe.hset(skey, 'when', when)
        pipe.hset(skey, 'delta', delta)
        pipe.hset(skey, 'total', total)
        pipe.hset(skey, 'runs', 0)
        pipe.hset(skey, 'errors', 0)
        pipe.hset(skey, 'cerrors', 0)
        pipe.hset(skey, 'status', 'running')
        pipe.execute()
        self.post_job(skey, when)
        return True

    def get_batch_schedule_status(self, user, pids):
        pipe = self.r.pipeline()
        for pid in pids:
            jkey = mk_sched_key('job', user, pid)
            pipe.hgetall(jkey)
        ss = pipe.execute()
        out = {}

        for pid, s in zip(pids,ss):
            if 'pid' in s:
                ps  = self.prep_status(s)
                out[ s['pid' ]] = ps
            else:
                out[pid] = {}
        return out


    def prep_status(self, status):
        skip_fields = set(['auth_code'])
        int_fields = set(['cerrors', 'delta', 'errors', 'next_run',
            'runs', 'total', 'when'])

        out = {}
        for k, v in status.items():
            if k in skip_fields:
                continue
            if k in int_fields:
                v = int(v)
            out[k] = v
        return out
        
    def post_job(self, skey, when):
        print('posting', skey, 'to run in', when - time.time(), 'secs')
        pipe = self.r.pipeline()
        pipe.hset(skey, 'status', 'queued')
        pipe.hset(skey, 'next_run', when)
        pipe.zadd(self.job_queue, {skey: when})
        pipe.lpush(self.wait_queue, 1)
        pipe.execute()
        self.pm.inc_global_counter("jobs_posted")

    def cancel(self, user, pid):
        skey = mk_sched_key('job', user, pid)
        self.r.zrem(self.job_queue, skey)
        pipe = self.r.pipeline()
        pipe.hset(skey, 'next_run', 0)
        pipe.hset(skey, 'status', 'stopped')
        pipe.execute()
        self.pm.inc_global_counter("jobs_canceled")
        return True

    def get_run_stats(self, user, pid):
        skey = mk_sched_key('job', user, pid)
        stats = self.r.hgetall(skey)
        return self.prep_status(stats)

    def get_recent_results(self, user, pid):
        rkey = mk_sched_key('results', user, pid)
        results = self.r.lrange(rkey, 0, self.max_retained_results - 1)
        out = []
        for js in results:
            out.append(json.loads(js))
        return out

    def get_next_item(self):
        now = self.now()
        items = self.r.zrange(self.job_queue, 0, 0, withscores=True, score_cast_func=int)
        if len(items) > 0:
            item = items[0]
            skey, next_time = item
            if now >= next_time:
                self.r.zrem(self.job_queue, skey)
                return skey
        else:
            return None

    def get_next_delta(self):
        now = self.now()
        items = self.r.zrange(self.job_queue, 0, 0, withscores=True, score_cast_func=int)
        if len(items) > 0:
            item = items[0]
            skey, next_time = item
            return next_time - now
        else:
            return self.max_time
        
    def wait_for_next(self):
        timeout = self.get_next_delta()
        if timeout > 0:
            print('waiting for', timeout, 'secs')
            self.r.blpop(self.wait_queue, timeout)
        return self.get_next_item()
            
    def execute_job(self, skey):
        results = None
        info = self.r.hgetall(skey)
        print('execute_job', skey, info)
        if info:
            print('execute_job', info)
            auth_code = info['auth_code']
            pid = info['pid']
            results = self.pm.execute_program(auth_code, pid, True)
            self.pm.inc_global_counter("jobs_executed")
        return results

    def run_job(self, skey):
        self.r.hset(skey, 'status', 'running')
        results = self.execute_job(skey)
        if results:
            self.process_job_result(skey, results)

    def process_job_result(self, skey, results):
        p = self.r.pipeline()
        p.hincrby(skey, 'runs', 1)
        if results['status'] == 'ok':
            p.hset(skey, 'cerrors', 0)
        else:
            p.hincrby(skey, 'cerrors', 1)
            p.hincrby(skey, 'errors', 1)
        p.hgetall(skey)
        pres = p.execute()
        info = pres[-1]

        cerrors = int(info['cerrors'])
        runs = int(info['runs'])
        delta = int(info['delta'])

        print()
        print('info', info)
        print()

        user = info['user']
        pid = info['pid']

        results['runtime'] = time.time()
        if cerrors > self.max_cerrors:
            results['info'] = 'max consecutive errors exceeded, job cancelled'
            self.r.hset(skey, 'next_run', 0)
            self.r.hset(skey, 'status', 'cancelled')
            self.pm.inc_global_counter("jobs_max_errors_reached")
        elif runs >= int(info['total']):
            results['info'] = 'total runs reached, job finished'
            self.r.hset(skey, 'status', 'finished')
            self.r.hset(skey, 'next_run', 0)
            self.pm.inc_global_counter("jobs_total_runs_reached")
        elif delta == 0:
            results['info'] = 'run cancelled by user'
            self.r.hset(skey, 'status', 'cancelled')
            self.r.hset(skey, 'next_run', 0)
            self.pm.inc_global_counter("jobs_cancelled_by_user")
        else:
            next_time = self.now() + delta
            next_date = datetime.fromtimestamp(next_time).strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
            results['info'] = 'next run at ' + next_date
            self.post_job(skey, next_time)

        ntracks = len(results['tids']) if 'tids' in results else 0
        results['oinfo'] = 'generated ' + str(ntracks) + ' tracks'
        rkey = mk_sched_key('results', user, pid)
        jresults = json.dumps(results, indent=2)
        # print jresults
        self.r.lpush(rkey, jresults)
        self.r.ltrim(rkey, 0, self.max_retained_results - 1)
        self.r.expire(rkey, self.max_age_results)
        show_results(results)


    def now(self):
        return int(time.time())

    def process_job_queue(self):
        print('starting job pusher')
        while True:
            skey = self.wait_for_next()
            if skey:
                print('    pushing', skey)
                self.r.rpush(self.proc_queue, skey)

    def process_jobs(self):
        print('starting job processor')
        while True:
            _,skey = self.r.blpop(self.proc_queue)
            if skey:
                print('   processing', skey)
                self.run_job(skey)
            else:
                break
        print('shutting down job processor')

    def start_processing_threads(self, threads=5):
        def worker():
            self.process_jobs()

        self.show_info()

        for i in range(threads):
            t = threading.Thread(target=worker)
            t.daemon = True
            t.start()
        self.process_job_queue()

    def show_info(self):
        count = self.r.zcount(self.job_queue, -sys.maxsize, sys.maxsize)
        print('job queue has', count, 'jobs')

        
def show_results(result):
    try:
        print("%s %s %.2f" % (result['status'], fmt_date(result['runtime']), result['time']))
        print(result['oinfo'])
        print(result['info'])
        if result['status'] == 'ok':
            print(result['name'])
            print(result['uri'])
        else:
            print(result['message'])
        print()
    except:
        raise
        print("trouble showing formatted result")
        print(json.dumps(result, indent=2))
        print()

def fmt_date(ts):
    the_date = date.fromtimestamp(ts)
    return the_date.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
        
        
def mk_sched_key(op, user, pid):
    return 'sched-' + op + '-' + user + '-' + pid

if __name__ == '__main__':
    import random
    import spotify_auth

    my_redis = redis.StrictRedis(host=os.environ.get('REDIS_HOST', 'localhost'), port=int(os.environ.get('REDIS_PORT', 6379)), db=0, decode_responses=True)
    my_auth = spotify_auth.SpotifyAuth(r=my_redis)
    my_pm = program_manager.ProgramManager(my_auth, r=my_redis)

    sched = Scheduler(my_redis, my_pm)

    threads = 5
    if len(sys.argv) > 1:
        threads = int(sys.argv[1])

    sched.start_processing_threads(threads)

The `web` and `scheduler` services use `build: .` — Docker caches the image and `restart: unless-stopped` just restarts the old image. You need to force a rebuild on the Synology.

SSH in and run:

```bash
cd /path/to/smarter-playlists-clone
git pull
docker compose build --no-cache web scheduler
docker compose up -d
```

Or if you want to keep Redis data intact and minimize downtime:

```bash
git pull
docker compose build web scheduler
docker compose up -d --force-recreate web scheduler
```

The `--no-cache` ensures the old layer cache is discarded. After this, the logs should show `[spotify_plugs]` lines and the `market=from_token` fix will be active.

The code fix is working (`market=from_token` is being sent). The 404 is a genuine Spotify API access restriction — as of late 2024, Spotify restricted third-party API access to personalized editorial playlists like Release Radar and Discover Weekly. These playlists return 404 even with a valid auth token.

This isn't fixable in code. The user needs to update their program to replace the Release Radar source with their personal Release Radar URI, which they can get directly from the Spotify app:

1. Open Spotify → go to Release Radar
2. Click ··· → Share → Copy link to playlist
3. Paste the URL into the SmarterPlaylists playlist source field instead of searching by name

The stored URI `37i9dQZEVXbgW2o23eKnnt` is a stale search result from before the API change. The user's actual personal Release Radar has a different ID.

We can at least give a clearer error message when this happens:

content.content:
1→# Spotify API Compatibility Update
     2→
     3→## Context
     4→
     5→SmarterPlaylists was originally built against the Spotify + Echo Nest APIs circa 2016. Several Spotify API endpoints and spotipy library methods have been deprecated since then. The Echo Nest API was shut down entirely in 2016. This plan updates all API integration to current Spotify Web API standards (2026) to prevent future breakage.
     6→
     7→---
     8→
     9→## Phase 1: Backend — `pbl/pbl/spotify_plugs.py`
    10→
    11→### 1a. Update deprecated spotipy method calls
    12→
    13→| Line | Old | New |
    14→|------|-----|-----|
    15→| 145 | `_get_spotify().user_playlists(user)` | `_get_spotify().user_playlists(user)` — keep as-is, used for arbitrary users |
    16→| 374 | `_, _, user, _, pid = self.uri.split(':')` | Handle both 3-part and 5-part URI formats |
    17→| 391 | `sp.user_playlist_create(self.user, ...)` | `sp.user_playlist_create(self.user, ...)` — still works in spotipy 2.23+ |
    18→| 401 | `sp.user_playlist_replace_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_replace_items(pid, turis)` |
    19→| 404 | `sp.user_playlist_add_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_add_items(pid, turis)` |
    20→| 435 | `sp.user_playlists(user, ...)` | `sp.current_user_playlists(...)` |
    21→
    22→### 1b. Fix `_save_playlist` URI parsing (line 374)
    23→
    24→Currently assumes old 5-part format `spotify:user:X:playlist:Y`. Update to handle both:
    25→```python
    26→parts = self.uri.split(':')
    27→if len(parts) == 5:
    28→    _, _, user, _, pid = parts
    29→elif len(parts) == 3:
    30→    _, _, pid = parts
    31→    user = self.user
    32→```
    33→
    34→Also fix line 393 which does `uri.split(':')[4]` — same issue.
    35→
    36→### 1c. Update `normalize_uri()` (line 616)
    37→
    38→Modern Spotify URLs are `https://open.spotify.com/playlist/Y` (no user segment). After URL→URI conversion, normalize old 5-part playlist URIs to 3-part:
    39→```python
    40→# After URL conversion, normalize old playlist URIs
    41→parts = uri.split(':')
    42→if len(parts) == 5 and parts[0] == 'spotify' and parts[1] == 'user' and parts[3] == 'playlist':
    43→    uri = 'spotify:playlist:' + parts[4]
    44→```
    45→
    46→### 1d. Safe access for deprecated response fields (lines 490, 565, 573)
    47→
    48→Use `.get()` with defaults for `popularity` (deprecated by Spotify):
    49→- `track.get('popularity', 0)`
    50→- `album.get('popularity', 0)`
    51→- `artist.get('popularity', 0)`
    52→
    53→---
    54→
    55→## Phase 2: Backend — `app/server/plugs.py`
    56→
    57→### 2a. Replace deprecated spotipy calls
    58→
    59→| Line | Old | New |
    60→|------|-----|-----|
    61→| 445 | `sp.user_playlist_replace_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_replace_items(pid, turis)` |
    62→| 447 | `sp.user_playlist_add_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_add_items(pid, turis)` |
    63→| 519 | `sp.user_playlist_add_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_add_items(pid, turis)` |
    64→| 573 | `sp.user_playlist_replace_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_replace_items(pid, turis)` |
    65→| 575 | `sp.user_playlist_add_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_add_items(pid, turis)` |
    66→| 767 | `get_spotify().user_playlists(user)` | `get_spotify().current_user_playlists()` |
    67→| 782 | `get_spotify().user_playlist_tracks(user, playlist_id, ...)` | `get_spotify().playlist_items(playlist_id, ...)` |
    68→| 899 | `get_spotify().user_playlists(user)` | `get_spotify().current_user_playlists()` |
    69→| 915 | `get_spotify().user_playlist_tracks(user, playlist_id, ...)` | `get_spotify().playlist_items(playlist_id, ...)` |
    70→
    71→Note: `user_playlist_create` (lines 435, 510, 559) still works in spotipy 2.23+ — keep as-is.
    72→
    73→---
    74→
    75→## Phase 3: Frontend — `app/web/callback.html`
    76→
    77→### 3a. Update API endpoint URLs
    78→
    79→| Line | Old | New |
    80→|------|-----|-----|
    81→| 30 | `/v1/users/{username}/playlists` | `/v1/me/playlists` |
    82→| 53-55 | `/v1/users/{username}/playlists/{pid}/tracks` | `/v1/playlists/{pid}/tracks` |
    83→| 87-88 | `/v1/users/{username}/playlists/{pid}/tracks` | `/v1/playlists/{pid}/tracks` |
    84→
    85→### 3b. Fix URI construction (line 138)
    86→
    87→Old: `'spotify:user:' + username + ':playlist:' + pid`
    88→New: `'spotify:playlist:' + pid`
    89→
    90→Also update the link to use web URL: `'https://open.spotify.com/playlist/' + pid`
    91→
    92→### 3c. Fix `doit()` URI parsing (lines 188-190)
    93→
    94→Handle both old 5-part and new 3-part URI formats when extracting pid from `g_uri`.
    95→
    96→---
    97→
    98→## Phase 4: Frontend — `app/web/playlist.js`
    99→
   100→### 4a. Handle deprecated `preview_url` gracefully (lines 53-63)
   101→
   102→`preview_url` is deprecated and may be `null`. Add null check before calling `play()`:
   103→```javascript
   104→if (track.spotify && track.spotify.preview_url) {
   105→    play(track.spotify.preview_url);
   106→} else {
   107→    fetchSpotifyTrackInfo(track.id, function(info) {
   108→        if (info && info.preview_url) {
   109→            track.spotify = info;
   110→            play(info.preview_url);
   111→        }
   112→        // silently fail if no preview available
   113→    });
   114→}
   115→```
   116→
   117→### 4b. Fix `fetchSpotifyTrackInfo` (line 70-78)
   118→
   119→This calls `GET /v1/tracks/{tid}` without auth — will fail. Add auth header using stored token, or remove this function since previews are unreliable now anyway.
   120→
   121→### 4c. Remove deprecated implicit grant `loginWithSpotify` (lines 86-92)
   122→
   123→Uses `response_type=token` (Implicit Grant, deprecated by Spotify). This function is unused by the main app — the auth flow uses `main.js`'s `loginWithSpotifyForAuth()` instead. Remove or mark as deprecated.

# Spotify API Compatibility Update

## Context

SmarterPlaylists was originally built against the Spotify + Echo Nest APIs circa 2016. Several Spotify API endpoints and spotipy library methods have been deprecated since then. The Echo Nest API was shut down entirely in 2016. This plan updates all API integration to current Spotify Web API standards (2026) to prevent future breakage.

---

## Phase 1: Backend — `pbl/pbl/spotify_plugs.py`

### 1a. Update deprecated spotipy method calls

| Line | Old | New |
|------|-----|-----|
| 145 | `_get_spotify().user_playlists(user)` | `_get_spotify().user_playlists(user)` — keep as-is, used for arbitrary users |
| 374 | `_, _, user, _, pid = self.uri.split(':')` | Handle both 3-part and 5-part URI formats |
| 391 | `sp.user_playlist_create(self.user, ...)` | `sp.user_playlist_create(self.user, ...)` — still works in spotipy 2.23+ |
| 401 | `sp.user_playlist_replace_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_replace_items(pid, turis)` |
| 404 | `sp.user_playlist_add_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_add_items(pid, turis)` |
| 435 | `sp.user_playlists(user, ...)` | `sp.current_user_playlists(...)` |

### 1b. Fix `_save_playlist` URI parsing (line 374)

Currently assumes old 5-part format `spotify:user:X:playlist:Y`. Update to handle both:
```python
parts = self.uri.split(':')
if len(parts) == 5:
    _, _, user, _, pid = parts
elif len(parts) == 3:
    _, _, pid = parts
    user = self.user
```

Also fix line 393 which does `uri.split(':')[4]` — same issue.

### 1c. Update `normalize_uri()` (line 616)

Modern Spotify URLs are `https://open.spotify.com/playlist/Y` (no user segment). After URL→URI conversion, normalize old 5-part playlist URIs to 3-part:
```python
# After URL conversion, normalize old playlist URIs
parts = uri.split(':')
if len(parts) == 5 and parts[0] == 'spotify' and parts[1] == 'user' and parts[3] == 'playlist':
    uri = 'spotify:playlist:' + parts[4]
```

### 1d. Safe access for deprecated response fields (lines 490, 565, 573)

Use `.get()` with defaults for `popularity` (deprecated by Spotify):
- `track.get('popularity', 0)`
- `album.get('popularity', 0)`
- `artist.get('popularity', 0)`

---

## Phase 2: Backend — `app/server/plugs.py`

### 2a. Replace deprecated spotipy calls

| Line | Old | New |
|------|-----|-----|
| 445 | `sp.user_playlist_replace_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_replace_items(pid, turis)` |
| 447 | `sp.user_playlist_add_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_add_items(pid, turis)` |
| 519 | `sp.user_playlist_add_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_add_items(pid, turis)` |
| 573 | `sp.user_playlist_replace_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_replace_items(pid, turis)` |
| 575 | `sp.user_playlist_add_tracks(user, pid, turis)` | `sp.playlist_add_items(pid, turis)` |
| 767 | `get_spotify().user_playlists(user)` | `get_spotify().current_user_playlists()` |
| 782 | `get_spotify().user_playlist_tracks(user, playlist_id, ...)` | `get_spotify().playlist_items(playlist_id, ...)` |
| 899 | `get_spotify().user_playlists(user)` | `get_spotify().current_user_playlists()` |
| 915 | `get_spotify().user_playlist_tracks(user, playlist_id, ...)` | `get_spotify().playlist_items(playlist_id, ...)` |

Note: `user_playlist_create` (lines 435, 510, 559) still works in spotipy 2.23+ — keep as-is.

---

## Phase 3: Frontend — `app/web/callback.html`

### 3a. Update API endpoint URLs

| Line | Old | New |
|------|-----|-----|
| 30 | `/v1/users/{username}/playlists` | `/v1/me/playlists` |
| 53-55 | `/v1/users/{username}/playlists/{pid}/tracks` | `/v1/playlists/{pid}/tracks` |
| 87-88 | `/v1/users/{username}/playlists/{pid}/tracks` | `/v1/playlists/{pid}/tracks` |

### 3b. Fix URI construction (line 138)

Old: `'spotify:user:' + username + ':playlist:' + pid`
New: `'spotify:playlist:' + pid`

Also update the link to use web URL: `'https://open.spotify.com/playlist/' + pid`

### 3c. Fix `doit()` URI parsing (lines 188-190)

Handle both old 5-part and new 3-part URI formats when extracting pid from `g_uri`.

---

## Phase 4: Frontend — `app/web/playlist.js`

### 4a. Handle deprecated `preview_url` gracefully (lines 53-63)

`preview_url` is deprecated and may be `null`. Add null check before calling `play()`:
```javascript
if (track.spotify && track.spotify.preview_url) {
    play(track.spotify.preview_url);
} else {
    fetchSpotifyTrackInfo(track.id, function(info) {
        if (info && info.preview_url) {
            track.spotify = info;
            play(info.preview_url);
        }
        // silently fail if no preview available
    });
}
```

### 4b. Fix `fetchSpotifyTrackInfo` (line 70-78)

This calls `GET /v1/tracks/{tid}` without auth — will fail. Add auth header using stored token, or remove this function since previews are unreliable now anyway.

### 4c. Remove deprecated implicit grant `loginWithSpotify` (lines 86-92)

Uses `response_type=token` (Implicit Grant, deprecated by Spotify). This function is unused by the main app — the auth flow uses `main.js`'s `loginWithSpotifyForAuth()` instead. Remove or mark as deprecated.

---

## Phase 5: Echo Nest Cleanup

### 5a. `pbl/pbl/echonest_plugs.py`

- **Comment out** the annotator registration at line 225: `tlib.add_annotator(_echonest_annotator)` — this registers a non-functional annotator that will fail when called
- Guard the `import pyen` with try/except so removal of pyen from requirements doesn't break imports
- Keep class definitions so existing saved programs get clear errors instead of import failures

### 5b. `app/server/components.py`

- Echo Nest components (EchoNestGenreRadio, EchoNestArtistRadio, EchoNestArtist) already have `'disabled': True` — no change needed
- Remove `"echonest"` from the annotations type list (around line 36) since it's non-functional

---

## Phase 6: Frontend Scopes — `app/web/main.js` + `main2.js`

- Fix duplicate `user-follow-read` scope (appears twice, lines 439-440)
- Optionally add `user-read-recently-played` scope

---

## Phase 7: `requirements.txt`

- Keep `spotipy>=2.23,<3.0` (already correct)
- Keep `pyen>=0.3` for now (echonest_plugs.py still imports it at module level; guarded with try/except in Phase 5)

---

## Files to Modify

1. `pbl/pbl/spotify_plugs.py` — deprecated spotipy methods, URI handling, deprecated fields
2. `app/server/plugs.py` — deprecated spotipy methods (12 call sites)
3. `app/web/callback.html` — old Spotify API endpoints, old URI format
4. `app/web/playlist.js` — deprecated preview_url, deprecated implicit grant
5. `pbl/pbl/echonest_plugs.py` — disable annotator registration
6. `app/server/components.py` — remove echonest from annotations list
7. `app/web/main.js` — fix duplicate scope
8. `app/web/main2.js` — fix duplicate scope

## Verification

1. Run local import test: `.venv/bin/python -c "import pbl; import components; import compiler; import plugs"` to verify no import errors
2. Rebuild Docker image and deploy to Synology
3. Test: login → create a simple playlist program → save → run → verify playlist appears in Spotify
4. Test: load existing program from directory → run
5. Check Docker logs for any Python errors after each operation

    15→import sys

    18→import simplejson as json

    21→
    22→class SpotifyAuth(object):
    23→
    24→    def __init__(self, r = None):
    25→        if r:
    26→            self.r = r
    27→        else:
    28→            self.r = redis.StrictRedis(host=os.environ.get('REDIS_HOST', 'localhost'), port=int(os.environ.get('REDIS_PORT', 6379)), db=0, decode_responses=True)
    29→        self.EXPIRES_THRESHOLD = 120
    30→        self.client_id = os.environ.get('SPOTIPY_CLIENT_ID')
    31→        self.client_secret = os.environ.get('SPOTIPY_CLIENT_SECRET')
    32→        self.client_redirect_uri = os.environ.get('SPOTIPY_REDIRECT_URI')
    33→        self.trace = False
    34→
    35→        print('client id', self.client_id)
    36→        print('client secret', self.client_secret)
    37→        print('client redirect uri', self.client_redirect_uri)
    38→
    39→        if self.client_id == None or self.client_secret == None or \
    40→            self.client_redirect_uri == None:
    41→            raise Exception('Missing SPOTIPY credentials in the environment')
    42→
    43→
    44→    def get_fresh_token(self, code):
    45→        now = time.time()
    46→        token = self._get_token(code)
    47→        if token:
    48→            if (token['expires_at'] - now) < self.EXPIRES_THRESHOLD:
    49→                token = self._refresh_token(token)
    50→                if token:
    51→                    self._add_token(code, token)
    52→        else:
    53→            token = self._add_auth_code(code)
    54→
    55→        return token
    56→
    57→    def get_fresh_token_for_user(self, user):
    58→        now = time.time()
    59→        token = self._get_token(user)
    60→        if token:
    61→            if (token['expires_at'] - now) < self.EXPIRES_THRESHOLD:
    62→                token = self._refresh_token(token)
    63→                if token:
    64→                    self._add_token(code, token)
    65→        return token
    66→
    67→    def _add_auth_code(self, auth_code):
    68→        token = self._get_new_token(auth_code)
    69→        if token:
    70→            token = self._add_token(auth_code, token)
    71→        return token
    72→
    73→    def _add_token(self, code, token):
    74→        now = time.time()
    75→        token['expires_at'] = int(now) + token['expires_in']
    76→        user_info = self._me(token)
    77→        if user_info and 'id' in user_info:
    78→            token['user_id'] = user_info['id']
    79→            token['user_name'] = user_info['display_name']
    80→
    81→            user = token['user_id']
    82→            self._put('token:' + code, token)
    83→            if self.trace:
    84→                print('added token to db', code, token)
    85→        else:
    86→            print("can't get user info, bailing")
    87→            return None
    88→        return token
    89→
    90→
    91→    def _get_new_token(self, authorization_code):
    92→        params = {
    93→            'grant_type': 'authorization_code',
    94→            'client_id': self.client_id,
    95→            'client_secret': self.client_secret,
    96→            'redirect_uri': self.client_redirect_uri,
    97→            'code' : authorization_code
    98→        }
    99→        r = requests.post('https://accounts.spotify.com/api/token', params)
   100→        if r.status_code >= 200 and r.status_code < 300:
   101→            token = r.json()
   102→            if self.trace:
   103→                print('got back token', token)
   104→            return token
   105→        else:
   106→            return None
   107→
   108→    def _get_token(self, code):
   109→        key = 'token:' + code
   110→        js = self._get(key)
   111→        return js
   112→
   113→    def _refresh_token(self, token):
   114→        params = {
   115→            'grant_type': 'refresh_token',
   116→            'client_id': self.client_id,
   117→            'client_secret': self.client_secret,
   118→            'refresh_token' : token['refresh_token']
   119→        }
   120→        r = requests.post('https://accounts.spotify.com/api/token', params)
   121→        if r.status_code >= 200 and r.status_code < 300:
   122→            new_token = r.json()
   123→            if self.trace:
   124→                print('got back token', token)
   125→            if not 'refresh_token' in new_token:
   126→                new_token['refresh_token'] = token['refresh_token']
   127→            return new_token
   128→        else:
   129→            raise Exception("can't get token")

   136→    def _spget(self, method, auth, params=None):
   137→        prefix = 'https://api.spotify.com/v1/'
   138→        args = dict(params=params)
   139→        url = prefix + method
   140→        headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer {0}'.format(auth)}
   141→        headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json'
   142→
   143→        r = requests.get(url, headers=headers, **args)
   144→
   145→        if len(r.text) > 0:
   146→            results = r.json()
   147→            if self.trace:  # pragma: no cover
   148→                print('RESP', results)
   149→                print()
   150→            return results
   151→        else:
   152→            return None
   153→
   154→    def _get(self, key):
   155→        js = self.r.get(key)
   156→        if js:
   157→            return json.loads(js)
   158→        else:
   159→            return None
   160→
   161→    def _put(self, key, val):
   162→        js = json.dumps(val)
   163→        self.r.set(key, js)

   165→    def delete_auth(self, code):
   166→        key = 'token:' + code
   167→        self.r.delete(key)

   111→class PlaylistSource(object):
   112→    '''
   113→        A PBL source that generates a stream of tracks from the given Spotify
   114→        playlist. If only a name is provided, the playlist will be searched for.
   115→        Search success can be improved if the owner of the playlist is also
   116→        provided.
   117→
   118→        :param name: the name of the playlist
   119→        :param uri: the uri of the playlist
   120→        :param user: the owner of the playlist
   121→
   122→    '''
   123→
   124→    def __init__(self, name, uri=None, user=None):
   125→        self.name = name
   126→        self.uri = normalize_uri(uri)
   127→        self.user = user
   128→
   129→        self.next_offset = 0
   130→        self.limit = 100
   131→
   132→        self.tracks = []
   133→        self.total = 1
   134→        self.cur_index = 0
   135→
   136→
   137→    def _get_uri_from_name(self, name):
   138→        results = _get_spotify().search(q=name, type='playlist')
   139→        if len(results['playlists']['items']) > 0:
   140→            return results['playlists']['items'][0]['uri']
   141→        else:
   142→            return None
   143→
   144→    def _get_uri_from_name_and_user(self, name, user):
   145→        results = _get_spotify().user_playlists(user)
   146→        while results:
   147→            for playlist in results['items']:
   148→                if playlist['name'].lower() == name.lower():
   149→                    return playlist['uri']
   150→            if results['next']:
   151→                results = _get_spotify().next(results)
   152→            else:
   153→                results = None
   154→        return None
   155→
   156→    def _get_more_tracks(self):
   157→        fields = self.uri.split(':')
   158→        if len(fields) == 5:
   159→            _,_,user,_,playlist_id = fields
   160→        else:
   161→            _,_,playlist_id = fields
   162→        print('[spotify_plugs] playlist_tracks uri=%s id=%s offset=%d' % (self.uri, playlist_id, self.next_offset))
   163→        try:
   164→            sp = _get_spotify()
   165→            print('[spotify_plugs] spotipy version=%s' % getattr(spotipy, '__version__', 'unknown'))
   166→            results = sp.playlist_tracks(playlist_id, limit=self.limit, offset=self.next_offset, market='from_token')
   167→        except spotipy.SpotifyException as e:
   168→            print('[spotify_plugs] SpotifyException http_status=%s reason=%s msg=%s' % (e.http_status, getattr(e, 'reason', '?'), e.msg))
   169→            if e.http_status == 404:
   170→                raise engine.PBLException(self, 'Playlist "%s" not found (id: %s). Spotify may have restricted API access to this playlist. Try using the direct Spotify URL instead of the playlist name.' % (self.name, playlist_id))
   171→            raise engine.PBLException(self, e.msg)
   172→
   173→        self.total = results['total']
   174→        for item in results['items']:
   175→            track = item['track']
   176→            if track and 'id' in track:
   177→                self.tracks.append(track['id'])
   178→                _add_track(self.name, track)
   179→        self.next_offset += self.limit
   180→
   181→    def next_track(self):
   182→        if self.uri == None:
   183→            if self.user:
   184→                self.uri = self._get_uri_from_name_and_user(self.name, self.user)
   185→            else:
   186→                self.uri = self._get_uri_from_name(self.name)
   187→
   188→            if not self.uri:
   189→                msg = "Can't find playlist named " + self.name
   190→                if self.user:
   191→                    msg += ' for user ' + self.user
   192→                raise engine.PBLException(self, msg)
   193→
   194→        if self.uri and self.cur_index >= len(self.tracks) \
   195→            and len(self.tracks) < self.total:
   196→            self._get_more_tracks()
   197→
   198→        if self.cur_index < len(self.tracks):
   199→            track = self.tracks[self.cur_index]
   200→            self.cur_index += 1
   201→            return track
   202→        else:
   203→            return None

1→# Spotify API Compatibility Update — Implementation Guide
     2→
     3→## Context
     4→
     5→SmarterPlaylists was built against the Spotify + Echo Nest APIs circa 2016. Several Spotify API endpoints and spotipy library methods have since been deprecated. The Echo Nest API was shut down entirely in 2016. This document details all changes needed to bring the codebase to current Spotify Web API standards (2026).
     6→
     7→---
     8→
     9→## 1. `pbl/pbl/spotify_plugs.py` — Core Spotify Backend
    10→
    11→### 1a. Fix `_save_playlist` URI parsing (line 374)
    12→
    13→**Problem:** Assumes old 5-part URI format `spotify:user:X:playlist:Y`.
    14→
    15→**Current:**
    16→```python
    17→_, _, user, _, pid = self.uri.split(':')
    18→```
    19→
    20→**New:**
    21→```python
    22→parts = self.uri.split(':')
    23→if len(parts) == 5:
    24→    _, _, user, _, pid = parts
    25→elif len(parts) == 3:
    26→    _, _, pid = parts
    27→    user = self.user
    28→else:
    29→    raise engine.PBLException(self, "bad playlist URI: " + self.uri)
    30→```
    31→
    32→### 1b. Fix playlist ID extraction after create (line 393)
    33→
    34→**Current:**
    35→```python
    36→pid = uri.split(':')[4]
    37→```
    38→
    39→**New:**
    40→```python
    41→parts = uri.split(':')
    42→pid = parts[4] if len(parts) == 5 else parts[2]
    43→```
    44→
    45→### 1c. Replace deprecated spotipy methods (lines 401, 404)
    46→
    47→**Current:**
    48→```python
    49→sp.user_playlist_replace_tracks(user, pid, turis)  # line 401
    50→sp.user_playlist_add_tracks(user, pid, turis)       # line 404
    51→```
    52→
    53→**New:**
    54→```python
    55→sp.playlist_replace_items(pid, turis)
    56→sp.playlist_add_items(pid, turis)
    57→```
    58→
    59→### 1d. Replace deprecated `_find_playlist_by_name` (line 435)
    60→
    61→**Current:**
    62→```python
    63→playlists = sp.user_playlists(user, limit=batch_size, offset=start)
    64→```
    65→
    66→**New:**
    67→```python
    68→playlists = sp.current_user_playlists(limit=batch_size, offset=start)
    69→```
    70→
    71→### 1e. Update `normalize_uri()` (lines 616-634)
    72→
    73→**Problem:** Modern Spotify URLs are `https://open.spotify.com/playlist/Y` (no user segment). Old 5-part playlist URIs should be normalized to 3-part.
    74→
    75→**Current:**
    76→```python
    77→def normalize_uri(uri):
    78→    if uri:
    79→        uri = uri.strip()
    80→        if uri.startswith('https://open.spotify.com'):
    81→            uri = uri.replace("https://open.spotify.com", "spotify")
    82→            uri = uri.replace("/", ":")
    83→    check_uri(uri)
    84→    return uri
    85→```
    86→
    87→**New:**
    88→```python
    89→def normalize_uri(uri):
    90→    if uri:
    91→        uri = uri.strip()
    92→        if uri.startswith('https://open.spotify.com'):
    93→            uri = uri.replace("https://open.spotify.com", "spotify")
    94→            uri = uri.replace("/", ":")
    95→        # Normalize old 5-part playlist URIs to modern 3-part format
    96→        parts = uri.split(':')
    97→        if len(parts) == 5 and parts[0] == 'spotify' and parts[1] == 'user' and parts[3] == 'playlist':
    98→            uri = 'spotify:playlist:' + parts[4]
    99→    check_uri(uri)
   100→    return uri
   101→```
   102→
   103→### 1f. Safe access for deprecated response fields (lines 490, 565, 573)
   104→
   105→Spotify has deprecated `popularity` on track/album/artist objects. Use `.get()` with defaults:
   106→
   107→**Line 490:**
   108→```python
   109→# Current:  ntrack['popularity'] = track['popularity']
   110→# New:
   111→ntrack['popularity'] = track.get('popularity', 0)
   112→```
   113→
   114→**Line 565:**
   115→```python
   116→# Current:  falbum['popularity'] = album['popularity']
   117→# New:
   118→falbum['popularity'] = album.get('popularity', 0)
   119→```
   120→
   121→**Line 573:**
   122→```python
   123→# Current:  fartist['popularity'] = artist['popularity']
   124→# New:
   125→fartist['popularity'] = artist.get('popularity', 0)
   126→```
   127→
   128→---
   129→
   130→## 2. `app/server/plugs.py` — App Server Spotify Layer
   131→
   132→### 2a. Replace deprecated playlist modification methods
   133→
   134→All these changes follow the same pattern: remove the `user` parameter, use new method names.
   135→
   136→**Lines 445, 573 — `user_playlist_replace_tracks`:**
   137→```python
   138→# Current:  sp.user_playlist_replace_tracks(user, pid, turis)
   139→# New:
   140→sp.playlist_replace_items(pid, turis)
   141→```
   142→
   143→**Lines 447, 519, 575 — `user_playlist_add_tracks`:**
   144→```python
   145→# Current:  sp.user_playlist_add_tracks(user, pid, turis)
   146→# New:
   147→sp.playlist_add_items(pid, turis)
   148→```
   149→
   150→### 2b. Replace deprecated playlist reading methods
   151→
   152→**Lines 767, 899 — `user_playlists`:**
   153→```python
   154→# Current:  results = get_spotify().user_playlists(user)
   155→# New:
   156→results = get_spotify().current_user_playlists()
   157→```
   158→
   159→**Lines 782-783, 915-916 — `user_playlist_tracks`:**
   160→```python

   162→# New:
   163→results = get_spotify().playlist_items(playlist_id, limit=self.limit, offset=self.next_offset)
   164→```
   165→
   166→### 2c. Note: Keep `user_playlist_create` as-is
   167→
   168→Lines 435, 510, 559 use `sp.user_playlist_create(user, name)`. This method still works in spotipy 2.23+ (it delegates internally). No change needed.
   169→
   170→---
   171→
   172→## 3. `app/web/callback.html` — Frontend Direct Spotify API
   173→
   174→### 3a. Update `createPlaylist` endpoint (line 30)
   175→
   176→**Current:**
   177→```javascript
   178→var url = 'https://api.spotify.com/v1/users/' + username + '/playlists';
   179→```
   180→
   181→**New:**
   182→```javascript
   183→var url = 'https://api.spotify.com/v1/me/playlists';
   184→```
   185→
   186→### 3b. Update `addTracksToPlaylist` endpoint (lines 53-55)
   187→
   188→**Current:**
   189→```javascript

   193→
   194→**New:**

   199→### 3c. Update `replaceTracksInPlaylist` endpoint (lines 87-88)
   200→
   201→**Current:**

   204→    '/playlists/' + playlist + '/tracks';

   206→
   207→**New:**

   210→```
   211→
   212→### 3d. Fix URI construction in `addedTracks` (line 138)
   213→
   214→**Current:**
   215→```javascript
   216→var uri = 'spotify:user:' + username + ':playlist:' + pid
   217→// ...

   226→```
   227→
   228→### 3e. Fix `doit()` URI parsing (lines 188-190)
   229→
   230→**Current:**
   231→```javascript
   232→if (g_uri) {
   233→    var username = g_uri.split(':')[2];

   253→
   254→## 4. `app/web/playlist.js` — Track Preview & Auth
   255→
   256→### 4a. Handle deprecated `preview_url` (lines 53-64)
   257→
   258→`preview_url` is deprecated by Spotify and may return `null`.
   259→
   260→**Current:**
   261→```javascript
   262→title.on('click', function() {
   263→    if (track.spotify && track.spotify.preview_url) {
   264→        play(track.spotify.preview_url);
   265→    } else {
   266→        fetchSpotifyTrackInfo(track.id, function(spotify_track_info) {
   267→            if (spotify_track_info) {
   268→                track.spotify = spotify_track_info;
   269→                play(track.spotify.preview_url);
   270→            }
   271→        });
   272→    }

   274→```
   275→
   276→**New:**
   277→```javascript
   278→title.on('click', function() {
   279→    if (track.spotify && track.spotify.preview_url) {
   280→        play(track.spotify.preview_url);
   281→    } else {
   282→        fetchSpotifyTrackInfo(track.id, function(spotify_track_info) {
   283→            if (spotify_track_info && spotify_track_info.preview_url) {
   284→                track.spotify = spotify_track_info;
   285→                play(spotify_track_info.preview_url);
   286→            }

   288→        });

   292→
   293→### 4b. Remove deprecated `loginWithSpotify` function (lines 86-92)
   294→
   295→Uses `response_type=token` (Implicit Grant — officially deprecated by Spotify). This function is unused by the main app (auth uses `main.js` → `loginWithSpotifyForAuth()` instead). Remove it entirely.
   296→

   301→//         '&response_type=token' +

   305→// }

   310→## 5. `pbl/pbl/echonest_plugs.py` — Dead Echo Nest Code
   311→

   313→
   314→Echo Nest API shut down in 2016. The annotator always fails.

1→# SmarterPlaylists — Synology Setup Guide
     2→
     3→## Voraussetzungen
     4→
     5→- Synology NAS mit DSM 7+
     6→- Docker / Container Manager installiert (Paketcenter)
     7→- SSH-Zugang zur Synology aktiviert
     8→- Gitea läuft auf `192.168.10.20:222`
     9→- Spotify-Account
    10→
    11→---
    12→
    13→## Phase 1 — Spotify Developer App
    14→
    15→### 1.1 App erstellen
    16→
    17→1. Gehe zu [developer.spotify.com/dashboard](https://developer.spotify.com/dashboard) und logge dich ein
    18→2. Klicke **Create app**
    19→3. Fülle aus:
    20→   - **App name:** `SmarterPlaylists`
    21→   - **App description:** beliebig
    22→   - **Redirect URI:** `http://<SYNOLOGY_IP>:59071/auth.html`
    23→     → z.B. `http://192.168.10.10:59071/auth.html`
    24→   - **APIs used:** Web API ✓
    25→4. Klicke **Save**
    26→
    27→### 1.2 Credentials kopieren
    28→
    29→Klicke in der App-Übersicht auf **Settings**:
    30→- **Client ID** → kopieren
    31→- **Client secret** → "View client secret" → kopieren
    32→
    33→---
    34→
    35→## Phase 2 — Synology vorbereiten
    36→
    37→### 2.1 SSH verbinden
    38→
    39→```bash
    40→ssh dein-user@192.168.10.x
    41→```
    42→
    43→### 2.2 Repo klonen
    44→
    45→```bash
    46→mkdir -p /volume1/docker/smarterplaylists
    47→cd /volume1/docker/smarterplaylists
    48→
    49→git clone ssh://git@192.168.10.20:222/gitea/smarter-playlists-clone.git .
    50→```

    53→

```python
class MyFollowedArtists(object):
    ''' A PBL Source that generates top tracks from followed artist
        by the current user
    '''

    def __init__(self, num_tracks):
        self.name = 'MyFollowedArtists'
        self.num_tracks = num_tracks
        self.buffer = None

    def next_track(self):
        if self.buffer == None:
            self.buffer = []
            try:
                sp = get_spotify()
                limit = 50
                after = None
                while True:
                    try:
                        results = get_spotify().current_user_followed_artists(limit = limit, after = after)
                    except spotipy.SpotifyException as e:
                        raise pbl.engine.PBLException(self, e.msg)

                    artists = results['artists']
                    items = artists['items']

                    for item in items:
                        artist_id = item['id']
                        after = artist_id
                        try:
                            results = get_spotify()._get('artists/' + artist_id + '/top-tracks')
                        except spotipy.SpotifyException as e:
                            raise pbl.engine.PBLException(self, e.msg)

                        for track in results['tracks'][:self.num_tracks]:
                            self.buffer.append(track['id'])
                            spotify_plugs._add_track(self.name, track)
                    if len(items) < limit:
                        break

            except spotipy.SpotifyException as e:
                raise pbl.engine.PBLException(self, e.msg)

        if len(self.buffer) > 0:
            return self.buffer.pop(0)
        else:
            return None
```

Perfect. Now I have all the information needed. Let me create a comprehensive report of my findings.

## Complete Analysis of the Re-login/Token Refresh Flow

Based on my thorough review of the SmarterPlaylists codebase, here are my detailed findings:

### 1. **auth.html - OAuth Callback & Auth Code Storage** 
(/Users/brunobrunkow/Downloads/SmarterPlaylists-master/app/web/auth.html, lines 59-83)

The OAuth callback is handled client-side:
- Spotify redirects to `auth.html` with the authorization code in the URL
- `initLogin()` function (lines 61-75) parses the URL parameters and extracts the `code`
- **The code is stored in localStorage** with key `'sp-auth-code'` (line 65)
- On success, the user is redirected to `go.html` (line 68)
- On error, an error message is displayed (line 71)

**Critical Note:** The auth code is stored in **browser localStorage**, not as a server-side session.

---

### 2. **spotify_auth.py - Token Storage & Refresh Logic**
(/Users/brunobrunkow/Downloads/SmarterPlaylists-master/app/server/spotify_auth.py)

#### Token Storage Key
- Tokens are stored in **Redis** with key: `'token:' + code` (line 82, 109)
- This means each unique auth code maps to exactly ONE token stored in Redis

#### `_add_auth_code()` (lines 67-71)
- Calls `_get_new_token()` to exchange the auth code for a token
- Stores the token via `_add_token()`

#### `_get_new_token()` (lines 91-106)
- Makes a POST request to Spotify's token endpoint with:
  - `grant_type: 'authorization_code'`
  - The provided `authorization_code`
  - Client ID and secret
  - Redirect URI
- Returns the raw token from Spotify API response (line 101)

#### `_add_token()` (lines 73-88) - **THIS IS CRITICAL**
- Calculates `expires_at` timestamp (line 75)
- Calls `_me()` to fetch user info from `/v1/me` endpoint (line 76)
- **ONLY stores user_id and user_name from the user info** (lines 78-79)
- **Does NOT store the `scope` field from the token**
- **Does NOT store the `country` field from `/v1/me` response**
- Stores the complete token in Redis (line 82)

#### `_refresh_token()` (lines 113-129)
- Used when a token is close to expiration
- Makes a refresh token request and returns new token
- **Does NOT preserve the `scope` field** (just passes through what Spotify returns)
- Does NOT fetch or update user country info

#### `get_fresh_token()` (lines 44-55)
- Retrieves existing token from Redis using the auth code
- If token exists and is fresh enough (not within 120 seconds of expiry), returns it
- If token is stale, calls `_refresh_token()` and updates Redis
- If no token exists, calls `_add_auth_code()` to get a new one

---

### 3. **flask_server.py - No Explicit /auth Endpoint**
(/Users/brunobrunkow/Downloads/SmarterPlaylists-master/app/server/flask_server.py)

**Finding:** There is **NO server-side `/auth` endpoint** that handles the OAuth code exchange. The code exchange happens entirely client-side via the browser's redirect to auth.html.

Instead, the Flask server relies on endpoints like:
- `/SmarterPlaylists/save`, `/SmarterPlaylists/directory`, `/SmarterPlaylists/program`, etc.
- These endpoints all call `auth.get_fresh_token(auth_code)` (lines 60, 90, 146, 176, 236, 279, 307, 398, 421, 475)
- They extract `auth_code` from the request parameters

#### `user_info()` endpoint (lines 415-432)
- Returns user info from the token: `user_id` and `user_name`
- **Does NOT return scope or country information**

---

### 4. **program_manager.py - Token Usage** 
(/Users/brunobrunkow/Downloads/SmarterPlaylists-master/app/server/program_manager.py, lines 251-340)

In `execute_program()` around line 259:
```python
token = self.auth.get_fresh_token(auth_code)  # line 259
...
delta = token['expires_at'] - time.time()     # line 265
pbl.engine.setEnv('spotify_auth_token', token['access_token'])  # line 271
pbl.engine.setEnv('spotify_user_id', token['user_id'])           # line 272
```

**Fields extracted from the token:**
- `token['expires_at']` - expiration timestamp
- `token['access_token']` - the actual API token
- `token['user_id']` - user identifier

**NOT extracted or used:**
- `token['scope']` - not accessed anywhere
- User's `country` field - not fetched or stored

---

### 5. **main.js - Logout & Re-login Flow**
(/Users/brunobrunkow/Downloads/SmarterPlaylists-master/app/web/main.js)

Logout handler (lines 364-366):
```javascript
$("#logout").on("click", function() {
    clear_auth_code();              // Removes 'sp-auth-code' from localStorage
    document.location = 'index.html'; // Redirects to login page
});
```

On error, if server returns 'no authorized user', the code automatically clears the auth code:
```javascript
if (data.status == 'error' && data.msg == 'no authorized user') {
    clear_auth_code();
    document.location = 'index.html';
}
```

---

## Analysis: Stale Token Issue After Re-login

### THE PROBLEM: Potential Token Stale-ness

**Scenario:** User logs out, then logs back in

1. **Logout:** `clear_auth_code()` removes `'sp-auth-code'` from browser localStorage
2. **Re-login:** User goes through Spotify OAuth flow again, gets a **new auth code**
3. **Token Storage:** New token is stored with key `'token:' + new_code`
4. **Old Token in Redis:** The old token with key `'token:' + old_code` remains in Redis indefinitely

**Critical Issue:** If an attacker or process somehow retrieves the old `auth_code`, they can still call `auth.get_fresh_token(old_code)` and get a valid token because:
- The old token is never deleted from Redis
- `_refresh_token()` will refresh it if expired
- There's **no mechanism to invalidate the old token**

### Scope Issue
- **Scope is NOT stored** in the token when initially added (line 77-79 only stores user_id and user_name)
- **Scope IS stored in the Spotify API response** (standard OAuth response includes scope)
- But the code never explicitly checks or validates that the correct scopes were granted
- If a user revokes scopes via Spotify settings and logs back in, the app will get a new token with fewer scopes, but there's no validation/error handling for missing scopes

### Country Issue
- **Country is NEVER fetched** from `/v1/me` response
- `_me()` gets the response but only extracts `id` and `display_name`
- If the app needed user's country, it would have to make a separate API call

---

## Summary

**Does the new token properly replace the old one on re-login?**

Functionally: **YES, mostly** - New re-login gets a fresh token that works fine

But with caveats:
1. The **old token remains in Redis** and is never cleaned up
2. There's **no token invalidation mechanism** - old tokens can still be refreshed if the code is reused
3. **Scope validation is absent** - if scopes change, the app won't know
4. **No logout server-side call** - Spotify's token revocation is not explicitly performed

This is a moderate security concern if auth codes can be intercepted or guessed.

# artist_top_tracks 403 — Root Cause & Fix

## Context

`GET /v1/artists/{id}/top-tracks` returns 403 even after re-login. Three layers of
investigation identified the root cause.

---

## Root Cause Analysis

### Layer 1 — Why `market='from_token'` returns 403
Spotify requires the `user-read-private` scope in the access token to resolve the user's
market from the token. We added `user-read-private` to the OAuth scope list in `main.js`,
but this only works if the user re-logs in **after** the JS file was updated on the server.

### Layer 2 — Why re-login may not have picked up the new scope
The nginx container serves static files directly from the host filesystem via volume mount
(`./app/web:/usr/share/nginx/html`). Static file changes (main.js) take effect immediately
**without a Docker rebuild**, but only if `git pull` was run on the Synology **before** the
user re-logged in. If the user re-logged in before or without `git pull`, the OAuth request
went out without `user-read-private` in the scope string, and the stored token still lacks
the scope.

### Layer 3 — Why no-market also returns 403
The Spotify API technically lists `market` as optional, but in practice their current API
version returns 403 for unauthenticated-market requests in some regions. Passing a concrete
country code (e.g. `'DE'`) avoids this ambiguity entirely, without needing `user-read-private`.

### Root fix
Stop relying on `market='from_token'`. Instead:
1. Fetch the user's country from `/v1/me` during auth and store it in the Redis token object.
2. Make it available in the pbl engine environment.
3. Use it as the `market` parameter in all `artist_top_tracks` calls.
4. Fall back to `'US'` if not available.

---

## Implementation Plan

### Step 1 — Store user country during auth
**File:** `app/server/spotify_auth.py`

In `_add_token()` (around line 73), `_me()` is already called to get user info. The `/v1/me`
response includes a `country` field (when the token was issued with `user-read-private`). Extract
and store it:

```python
# existing: token['user_id'] = me['id']
# existing: token['user_name'] = me.get('display_name', me['id'])
token['country'] = me.get('country', 'US')   # add this
```

### Step 2 — Pass country into pbl engine environment
**File:** `app/server/program_manager.py`

After line 272 (`setEnv('spotify_user_id', ...)`), add:
```python
pbl.engine.setEnv('spotify_user_country', token.get('country', 'US'))
```

### Step 3 — Use country as market in artist_top_tracks
**Files:** `app/server/plugs.py` and `pbl/pbl/spotify_plugs.py`

Add a helper to `plugs.py`:
```python
def get_user_market():
    country = pbl.engine.getEnv('spotify_user_country')
    if country:
        return country
    try:
        return get_spotify().current_user()['country']
    except Exception:
        return 'US'
```

Then update all three artist_top_tracks call sites:

| File | Line | Old | New |
|------|------|-----|-----|
| `app/server/plugs.py` | ~651 | `_get('artists/' + artist_id + '/top-tracks')` | `_get('artists/' + artist_id + '/top-tracks', market=get_user_market())` |
| `app/server/plugs.py` | ~1365 | `_get('artists/' + seed_uri + '/top-tracks')` | `_get('artists/' + seed_uri + '/top-tracks', market=get_user_market())` |
| `pbl/pbl/spotify_plugs.py` | ~332 | `_get('artists/' + id + '/top-tracks')` | `_get('artists/' + id + '/top-tracks', market=get_user_market())` — needs `engine.getEnv` directly since no `pbl.engine` alias |

For `spotify_plugs.py`, use `engine.getEnv('spotify_user_country') or 'US'` directly
since there's no `get_user_market()` helper there.

### Step 4 — Graceful per-artist error handling in MyFollowedArtists
**File:** `app/server/plugs.py`

Currently, if one artist fails the entire program crashes. Wrap the per-artist call to
skip on 403/404 instead:

```python
try:
    results = get_spotify()._get('artists/' + artist_id + '/top-tracks', market=get_user_market())
    for track in results['tracks'][:self.num_tracks]:
        ...
except spotipy.SpotifyException as e:
    print('[plugs] skipping artist %s: %s' % (artist_id, e.msg))
    continue  # skip this artist, don't crash the whole run
```

### Step 5 — Add scope logging for future debugging
**File:** `app/server/program_manager.py`

After retrieving the token, log what scopes it was issued with:
```python
print('[program_manager] token scopes:', token.get('scope', 'unknown'))
print('[program_manager] token country:', token.get('country', 'not set'))
```

---

## Files to Modify

1. `app/server/spotify_auth.py` — store `country` from `/v1/me` in token
2. `app/server/program_manager.py` — set `spotify_user_country` env + scope logging
3. `app/server/plugs.py` — add `get_user_market()` helper, use in both call sites, graceful per-artist error handling
4. `pbl/pbl/spotify_plugs.py` — use `engine.getEnv('spotify_user_country')` in `ArtistTopTracks`

---

## Deployment Note

After deploying, **existing tokens in Redis won't have the `country` field** (they were stored
before this change). The fallback path (`current_user()['country']` → `'US'`) handles this
transparently — no re-login required. New logins will store country in the token.

---
